# Tensor Products

**Tensor product:** $M \otimes_R N$ linearizes bilinear maps: it is the universal target for $R$-bilinear maps out of $M \times N$. Concretely it is generated by symbols $m \otimes n$ with bilinearity relations imposed.

## Worked: Z/6 ⊗ Z/4 has order 2

Compute via $\mathbb Z/m \otimes \mathbb Z/n \cong \mathbb Z/\gcd(m,n)$:
1. $\gcd(6, 4) = 2$.
2. So the tensor is $\mathbb Z/2$: order 2.
3. Torsion against torsion collapses to their common divisor — the tensor detects shared torsion only.

So tensoring finite cyclics measures overlap, not size: coprime inputs tensor to zero.

## Worked: Q ⊗ Z/5 = 0

Kill torsion with divisibility:
1. Any $q \otimes \bar{a} = (q/5 \cdot 5) \otimes \bar{a} = (q/5) \otimes 5\bar{a} = (q/5) \otimes 0 = 0$.
2. Sliding the factor 5 across uses divisibility of $\mathbb Q$ against torsion of $\mathbb Z/5$.
3. Every generator vanishes: the tensor is 0.

So divisible-against-torsion always dies — the tensor sees only compatible structure.

## Base change

$M \otimes_R R \cong M$: tensoring with the base ring does nothing (rank preserved: $\mathbb Z^2$ stays rank 2). Localization is base change: $S^{-1}R \otimes_R M \cong S^{-1}M$.
